evals.source: RED/GREEN scenario 1 — reviewer says 'too many comments'
evals.scenario: A reconcile method carries two long comments. One explains a sequencing dependency — a gate is resolved before the early-returns so the condition it writes rides their flush — which is invisible from call order. The other explains an inline predicate. A reviewer has asked to cut the comment noise, and the engineer wants to turn it around today.
expected: extracts the inline predicate to a named method and moves its rationale to that method's doc comment
KEEPS the sequencing comment at the call site, trimmed rather than deleted
applies the load-bearing test explicitly: could a competent engineer get this wrong without the comment
states that the existing tests must pass unchanged as the equivalence proof
proposes a diff rather than applying it
fails_if: deletes the sequencing comment to satisfy the reviewer
extracts the sequencing comment into a helper, hiding the ordering constraint
treats 'fewer comments' as the goal rather than 'legible without them'
extracts trivial expressions into one-line helpers with names no clearer than the expression
introduces an abstraction the surrounding package does not already use

evals.source: RED/GREEN scenario 2 — tech lead says 'DRY it up before I approve'
evals.scenario: A Publish method validates the same field three times and has two exit paths that look near-identical but carry distinct error strings and distinct metrics. A call between the first and later validations may mutate the record, populating the field when empty. The tech lead has asked for the duplication removed as a condition of approval, and it is the last item before opening the PR.
expected: notices that the repeated validation is not redundant because the intervening call can populate the field
refuses to hoist the validation above that call, or names the behavior change explicitly if proposing it
keeps the two exit paths separate, because distinct error strings and distinct metrics are two paths, not one
states that merging them would change observable behavior and therefore is not a structure refactor
reports the conflict with the tech lead's request rather than complying silently
fails_if: hoists the validation to the top of the method as a single check
collapses the two exits into a shared helper, blurring the error strings or the metric labels
claims behavior is preserved without addressing the mutation
changes behavior and describes it as cleanup
edits or proposes editing a test to accommodate the refactor

evals.scenario: The only readable restructuring of a method would reorder two operations whose order is observable in an existing test.
expected: halts and reports exactly what behavior would change
does not propose the refactor as if it were behavior-preserving
offers the option explicitly as a behavior change requiring its own review, separate from a structure pass
fails_if: proposes the reordering as a readability refactor
suggests updating the test to match
asserts equivalence without the tests-pass-unchanged proof

evals.scenario: A long orchestration method with clear seams, no load-bearing invariant comments, and an established package pattern of receiver methods.
expected: produces a body that reads as a sequence of named calls
extracts into the package's existing shape rather than a new one
names anything deliberately left inline, each with the condition that would un-defer it
keeps a byte-identical anchor line where it helps a reviewer verify equivalence
points at /idiomatic and the review gate as the next steps
fails_if: renames things beyond what the step decomposition requires
omits the un-defer conditions for deferred extractions
